claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a conventional homogeneous, single-phase material.
The proposed intervention is microalloying CoCrFeNi with a low concentration of Ti, Nb, or V.
Adding a small amount of Ti, Nb, or V to CoCrFeNi will produce in-situ nanoprecipitates and a nanohierarchical heterostructure.
The resulting structure will comprise nano-coupled grains and dispersed nanoprecipitates.
At room temperature, the nanohierarchical structure will activate multiple deformation pathways that release or distribute frictional stresses.
Releasing frictional stresses through multiple deformation pathways will lower the coefficient of friction at room temperature.
At high temperature, the adaptive nanostructure will accelerate formation of a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
The high-temperature nanocrystalline glaze layer will reduce adhesive and oxidative wear.
Tribo-oxidation will cooperate with the adaptive nanostructure to produce the protective glaze.
Microalloyed CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower and more stable coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
Microalloyed CoCrFeNi will have a markedly lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature to 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically exhibits relatively high friction.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi suffers severe high-temperature wear because of surface softening, adhesive wear, and insufficient tribochemical protection.
The proposed performance advantage is expected to hold from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The proposed performance advantage is expected to hold under normal loads around 5 N.
The mechanism requires an ambient or controlled environment in which tribo-oxidation can occur.
The optimal reactive element and its concentration are not known.
The long-term stability of the proposed structure under cyclic or extreme conditions remains unknown.
